Title: Account registration
Requirement: A person can create a platform account with email verification.
Evidence source: raw-audit/01-executive-summary.md (authenticated account exists; registration flow itself not observed)
Acceptance criteria: New account can sign in and reach an empty portfolio; unverified email cannot activate autonomous work.
Failure behavior: Clear error on duplicate email or failed verification; no partial account left usable.
Open question: Exact Polsia registration flow was not observed (audit used an existing session).

Title: Authentication and session
Requirement: Users authenticate with credentials and receive a server-managed session; all API access requires a valid session.
Acceptance criteria: Unauthenticated requests to any company resource are rejected; session expiry forces re-login without data loss.
Failure behavior: Failed logins are rate-limited and audited.

Title: Profile settings
Requirement: Users can edit profile details (name, email, content language) and save changes.
Acceptance criteria: Changes persist and are reflected across sessions; email change requires re-verification.
Failure behavior: Validation errors shown inline; no silent failure.

Title: Account deactivation
Requirement: Users can deactivate their account; deactivation stops all autonomous work and takes public artifacts offline.
Evidence source: raw-audit/02-application-map.md (Deactivate Account with warning); raw-audit/09-claim-verification.md claim 22
Acceptance criteria: After deactivation no scheduled or autonomous work runs; reactivation path is documented; data retained per retention policy.
Failure behavior: In-flight work is cancelled or completed safely and recorded.

Title: Account deletion
Requirement: Users can permanently delete their account and data after a cooling-off window, subject to legal retention.
Evidence source: Audit risk R-12 (ambiguous deletion); privacy baseline
Acceptance criteria: Deletion requires two-step confirmation and an export offer; after purge no personal data remains in active systems; audit record of the deletion event persists in redacted form.
Failure behavior: Deletion is blocked with explanation if legal holds exist.

Title: Company portfolio
Requirement: Users see a portfolio listing their companies with key status metrics.
User value: One place to oversee all ventures.
Acceptance criteria: Portfolio lists only the user's companies with status and headline metrics; empty state guides creation.
Failure behavior: Load failure shows retry without exposing other tenants' data.

Title: Multiple companies
Requirement: An account can hold multiple companies simultaneously.
Acceptance criteria: A second company can be created and both remain independently operable.
Failure behavior: Creation failure leaves no orphaned company shell.

Title: Company switching
Requirement: Users switch between companies without cross-contamination of context.
Acceptance criteria: Switching changes all visible data to the selected company only; no data from another company appears.
Failure behavior: Stale context is discarded on switch; errors force reload rather than mixed state.

Title: Portfolio metrics
Requirement: Portfolio rows show per-company summary metrics (e.g., activity, tasks, revenue placeholder) with source and freshness.
Acceptance criteria: Metrics show value, source, timestamp, and distinguish zero from unknown.
Failure behavior: Metric pipeline failure shows 'unavailable' state, never fabricated values.

Title: Company creation modes
Requirement: Users can start a company from (a) their own idea, (b) a platform-suggested idea, or (c) an existing business description.
Acceptance criteria: All three modes reachable from creation entry; idea mode is fully functional in MVP; each persists a company brief.
Failure behavior: Abandoned creation leaves a resumable draft, not a broken company.
Open question: Exact Polsia form content unknown (paid gate blocked inspection).

Title: Workspace provisioning
Requirement: Creating a company provisions a workspace: profile, mission draft, research area, roadmap area, document store, and activity stream. (Code/hosting provisioning is Post-MVP; see BUILD/DEPLOY.)
User value: A usable company workspace from minute one.
Acceptance criteria: After creation the workspace exposes profile, documents, tasks, and activity; every provisioning step is visible and resumable.
Failure behavior: A failed step is shown with reason and retry; no orphaned resources.

Title: Provisioning progress stream
Requirement: Provisioning progress is shown as an ordered, timestamped activity stream ending in an explicit completed or failed state.
Acceptance criteria: Each stage is timestamped and ordered; completion or failure is explicit; no stage claims success without a recorded result.
Failure behavior: Interrupted provisioning resumes from the last checkpoint.

Title: Company profile and brief
Requirement: Each company has an editable profile: name, brief, mission, market summary, and status.
User value: The company's identity in one place.
Acceptance criteria: Profile fields are editable with version history; edits create audit events.
Failure behavior: Concurrent edits resolve last-write-wins with visible history.

Title: Company settings
Requirement: Users can rename a company and manage company-level settings.
Acceptance criteria: Rename persists everywhere the name is displayed.
Failure behavior: Invalid names rejected with clear message.

Title: Company pause
Requirement: Users can pause a company; pause stops all scheduled and autonomous work without deleting data.
Acceptance criteria: While paused no new autonomous work starts; in-flight tasks reach a safe stop; resume restores schedules; both transitions are audited.
Failure behavior: Pause during an in-flight run reaches a defined safe state (see open question OQ-14).
Open question: Polsia's in-flight pause semantics are unknown.

Title: Company deletion safeguards
Requirement: Company deletion is a two-step confirmed, irreversible action with an export offer and audit trail.
Acceptance criteria: Deletion requires explicit typed confirmation; export is offered first; deletion event is audited; purge follows retention policy.
Failure behavior: Partial deletion failures roll forward to complete or restore a consistent state.

Title: Company status indicator
Requirement: Each company shows a human-readable operating status (e.g., provisioning, active, paused).
Acceptance criteria: Status reflects actual lifecycle state and updates within one minute of change.
Failure behavior: Unknown states render as 'unknown', never a fabricated healthy state.

Title: Adaptive interview engine
Requirement: The founder interview asks a small batch of questions at a time (max 3) and generates the next batch from previous answers.
User value: No overwhelming forms; relevant questions only.
Evidence source: polsia-audit-review.md ('adaptive founder interview' listed as NOT verified Polsia parity; our differentiator)
Acceptance criteria: No screen shows more than 3 questions; at least one later question demonstrably depends on an earlier answer; session state persists.
Failure behavior: Engine fallback to a static question set if generation fails, flagged as non-adaptive.

Title: Context-aware follow-ups
Requirement: The interview asks follow-up questions that reference and build on specific earlier answers.
Acceptance criteria: Follow-ups quote or reference the triggering answer; irrelevant follow-ups can be dismissed with reason captured.
Failure behavior: If context retrieval fails the question is asked generically and marked as such.

Title: Vague-answer detection
Requirement: The system detects vague or non-committal answers and asks for specifics with examples.
Acceptance criteria: A vague answer (e.g., 'everyone' as target customer) triggers one clarifying prompt with 2+ concrete examples; user may decline.
Failure behavior: Repeated vagueness is recorded as an explicit assumption, not silently accepted.

Title: Contradiction detection
Requirement: The interview detects contradictions between answers and surfaces them for resolution.
Acceptance criteria: A seeded contradictory answer pair is flagged with both statements shown; user resolves or accepts the tension explicitly.
Failure behavior: Undetected contradictions can be flagged manually later (UNDER-002).

Title: Unknown answers and suggested assumptions
Requirement: Users can answer 'I don't know'; the system proposes a labeled assumption with rationale that the user can accept, edit, or defer.
Acceptance criteria: 'I don't know' is always available; accepted assumptions are stored as Assumption memory items with source='AI-suggested'.
Failure behavior: Deferred questions appear in the understanding document as open items.

Title: Question rationale
Requirement: Each interview question can explain why the information matters and what it affects.
User value: Respects the founder's time and intelligence.
Acceptance criteria: Every question has a 'why we ask' affordance with a specific downstream use.
Failure behavior: Missing rationale defaults to a category-level explanation.

Title: Progressive resumable session
Requirement: The interview is resumable across sessions and never forces completion in one sitting.
Acceptance criteria: Closing mid-interview and returning restores position and answers exactly; progress indicator is honest.
Failure behavior: Corrupted session state recovers to the last confirmed answer.

Title: Answer correction
Requirement: Users can revise any earlier answer; dependent questions and assumptions are re-evaluated and flagged.
Acceptance criteria: Editing an answer marks dependent understanding items as needing review; nothing silently stays stale.
Failure behavior: Re-evaluation failure flags affected items as 'stale' visibly.

Title: Business-understanding document
Requirement: The system produces an editable structured understanding: idea, problem, target customer, user, buyer, solution, market, geography, language, business model, pricing assumptions, existing resources, budget, timeline, founder involvement, risk tolerance, constraints.
User value: One agreed picture of the business before any execution.
Evidence source: polsia-audit-review.md improvement 2 (explicit facts/assumptions not verified in Polsia)
Acceptance criteria: All listed fields exist; each is populated, marked unknown, or marked assumed; document renders in under 2s.
Failure behavior: Generation failure produces a partial document with missing sections explicitly labeled.

Title: Fact/assumption/preference separation
Requirement: Every understanding item is classified as confirmed fact, preference, constraint, AI assumption, research finding, or open question, with confidence.
User value: No conflation of what's known vs guessed.
Acceptance criteria: Each item shows class and confidence; filtering by class works; AI assumptions are visually distinct.
Failure behavior: Unclassifiable items default to 'open question', never to 'fact'.

Title: Understanding review controls
Requirement: Users can approve, edit, reject, request evidence, or request more research on any understanding item.
Acceptance criteria: All five actions are available per item; approval state is persisted and audited; execution planning is blocked until overall approval.
Failure behavior: Rejected items return to the interview flow for re-elicitation.

Title: Assumption lifecycle
Requirement: Assumptions carry status (proposed, accepted, validated, invalidated) and can be marked for future validation.
Acceptance criteria: Assumption status transitions are audited; 'validate later' creates a visible follow-up item.
Failure behavior: Invalidated assumptions flag dependent strategy/plan items for review.

Title: Understanding confidence display
Requirement: The understanding document shows overall and per-section confidence derived from item classes.
Acceptance criteria: Confidence updates when items change; method is documented in-product.
Failure behavior: Confidence never displays higher than the weakest Must-have section.

Title: Distinct strategic options
Requirement: After understanding approval the system generates at least 3 genuinely distinct strategic options (different customer, offer, or model — not cosmetic variants).
User value: Real choice instead of a single AI opinion.
Evidence source: raw-audit/09-claim-verification.md claim 23 (multiple options NOT found in Polsia, <50%)
Acceptance criteria: 3+ options differ on at least one of customer/offer/model; a similarity check rejects near-duplicates; generation completes within 5 minutes.
Failure behavior: Fewer than 3 viable options is stated honestly with reasons rather than padded.

Title: Option content standard
Requirement: Each option includes description, customer, offer, business model, product scope, benefits, risks, cost range, effort, time to validate, time to launch, required resources, key assumptions, validation method, success metrics, and confidence.
Acceptance criteria: All 16 fields present per option; cost/time fields use ranges with stated basis, never fake precision.
Failure behavior: Fields the system cannot estimate are marked 'unknown' with what would resolve them.

Title: Option selection controls
Requirement: Users can select, edit, combine, or reject options, or request another option.
Acceptance criteria: All five controls work; a combined option is re-rendered in the standard format for confirmation.
Failure behavior: Rejection of all options routes back to understanding review with captured reasons.

Title: AI recommendation with rationale
Requirement: The system may recommend one option, always with explicit rationale and its key sensitivities.
Acceptance criteria: Recommendation shows why, what would change it, and never auto-selects.
Failure behavior: Absent a defensible rationale, no recommendation is shown.

Title: Phase-limited approval
Requirement: Users can approve only the first phase of a strategy rather than the whole plan.
Acceptance criteria: Phase-only approval generates tasks solely for that phase; later phases remain visibly 'not approved'.
Failure behavior: Work generation respects the approval boundary; violations are blocked server-side.

Title: Decision record
Requirement: Every strategy selection/edit/rejection creates a durable decision record linking inputs, options considered, and rationale.
Acceptance criteria: Decision records are immutable, timestamped, linked to the understanding version, and visible in history.
Failure behavior: Failed record writes block the transition (decision is not silently unrecorded).

Title: Decision Room hub
Requirement: A single surface shows: needs-your-decision, recommended next actions, questions from the AI team, options under consideration, approved and queued, executing, results, blocked, failed, and recent decisions.
Acceptance criteria: All ten queues render with correct counts; every item deep-links to its full context; empty states are honest.
Failure behavior: Queue load failure degrades per-section, never renders wrong-company items.

Title: Autonomous task planning
Requirement: The system reviews company state and generates prioritized tasks with descriptions and types.
User value: The AI team proposes concrete work.
Acceptance criteria: Planning produces 3+ prioritized tasks linked to the selected strategy; each has type and description; planning is visible in the activity feed.
Failure behavior: Planning failure is visible with reason; no phantom tasks.

Title: User-steered planning
Requirement: Users can direct planning through a chat/planning surface (e.g., ask for tasks toward a goal).
Evidence source: raw-audit/04-task-and-agent-system.md (FAQ chat-run claim, 85%); raw-audit/02-application-map.md (chat surface observed)
Acceptance criteria: A natural-language planning request produces relevant tasks or an honest refusal; intent and effect are previewed before task creation.
Failure behavior: Ambiguous requests trigger clarification, not guessed execution.

Title: Recurring planning cycles
Requirement: Planning re-runs on a schedule, reviewing progress and generating next tasks.
Acceptance criteria: Scheduled cycles record review inputs, produced tasks, and completion; missed cycles are visible.
Failure behavior: Cycle failure alerts the owner and retries within policy.
Open question: Polsia's cycle internals (budget, stop conditions) are unknown.

Title: Planning transparency
Requirement: Each planning run shows what inputs it considered (memory items, metrics, prior results) and why the top tasks were chosen.
Acceptance criteria: Every planning run links its input snapshot and a rationale per proposed task.
Failure behavior: Missing rationale renders as 'not recorded' and counts against quality metrics.

Title: Goals roadmap and milestones
Requirement: Selecting a strategy generates goals, a roadmap, milestones, and initial tasks, stored as living documents.
Acceptance criteria: Roadmap contains goals, milestones with target sequencing, and generated tasks trace to milestones.
Failure behavior: Generation failure preserves the approved strategy and retries; partial roadmaps are labeled.

Title: Roadmap revision
Requirement: Roadmaps are versioned and editable; changes flag affected tasks and record rationale.
Acceptance criteria: Edits create versions with author and reason; affected open tasks are flagged for review.
Failure behavior: Version write failure blocks the edit rather than losing history.

Title: Task state machine
Requirement: Tasks move through defined states: To Do, Recurring, In Progress, Completed, Rejected, Failed (plus Cancelled).
Acceptance criteria: All state transitions are server-enforced, audited, and visible; invalid transitions are rejected.
Failure behavior: Stuck tasks time out to Failed with reason.

Title: Task detail
Requirement: Each task exposes type, creation time, structured description, and controls appropriate to its state.
User value: Understand any unit of work at a glance.
Acceptance criteria: Detail view shows all fields; controls reflect state and permissions.
Failure behavior: Missing fields render explicitly as missing.

Title: Scheduled autonomous work
Requirement: The platform supports scheduled task execution windows ('night shifts') with a monthly allowance.
Acceptance criteria: Scheduled runs occur in the configured window, respect policies, decrement allowance, and record results; owner can disable.
Failure behavior: Missed windows are reported; no silent skips.
Open question: What one scheduled shift may include needs owner definition (OQ-13).

Title: Manual task execution with credit preflight
Requirement: Users can run a task on demand; a preflight shows credit cost and expected side effects before execution; execution consumes one task credit.
Evidence source: raw-audit/24-runtime-billing-quality-validation.md (observed run consumed a credit); raw-audit/09-claim-verification.md claim 5
Acceptance criteria: Preflight shows cost and side-effect class; insufficient credits block execution with a clear path to resolve; ledger entry is atomic with the run.
Failure behavior: Execution failure refunds or preserves the credit per documented rule and shows which applied.

Title: Task result artifacts
Requirement: Completed tasks produce persistent result artifacts (documents/reports) linked from the task and the document library.
Acceptance criteria: Every Completed task links at least one artifact or an explicit 'no artifact' rationale; artifacts carry provenance (task, worker, inputs, time).
Failure behavior: Artifact persistence failure fails the task rather than reporting hollow success.

Title: Failure detail
Requirement: Failed tasks show an understandable error reason, what was attempted, whether retry is safe, and suggested next steps.
Evidence source: raw-audit/04-task-and-agent-system.md (Polsia failed task had NO visible error detail); raw-audit/19-competitive-gaps.md
Acceptance criteria: Every Failed task shows reason category, human-readable summary, attempt count, and retry safety; support bundle is exportable.
Failure behavior: Unknown causes are labeled 'unknown cause' with diagnostic reference, never blank.

Title: Task cancellation and pause
Requirement: Users can cancel a queued task and request stop of an in-progress task; the system reaches a defined safe state.
Evidence source: raw-audit/04-task-and-agent-system.md (controls not exercised in Polsia); company Pause observed
Acceptance criteria: Cancel on queued tasks is immediate; stop requests on running tasks reach safe-stop within a bounded time; both are audited.
Failure behavior: Uncancellable critical sections complete then honor the stop; state is truthful throughout.

Title: Repeat and delete controls
Requirement: Tasks can be repeated (re-queued as a new task) or deleted, with confirmation for delete.
Acceptance criteria: Repeat creates a linked new task; delete requires confirmation and is audited.
Failure behavior: Delete of a running task is refused; cancel first.

Title: Idempotent execution
Requirement: Task runs are idempotent: a retried or duplicate-triggered run never duplicates an external side effect.
User value: No double sends, double spends, double posts.
Acceptance criteria: Replay tests show zero duplicate external side effects; every external write carries an idempotency key.
Failure behavior: Detected duplicates are suppressed and logged as incidents.

Title: Visible retry policy
Requirement: Automatic retries (where enabled) are visible: attempt count, backoff, max attempts, and next attempt time.
User value: No hidden thrashing or silent giving-up.
Evidence source: raw-audit/09-claim-verification.md claim 28 (auto-retry NOT found in Polsia)
Acceptance criteria: Task detail shows retry configuration and history; retries respect idempotency.
Failure behavior: Exhausted retries move the task to Failed with full history.

Title: Worker registry
Requirement: The platform maintains a registry of AI workers with declared capabilities, allowed tools, and status.
Evidence source: polsia-audit-review.md (fixed agent count NOT verified in Polsia; capability labels only)
Acceptance criteria: Registry lists each worker with capabilities and tool allowlist; tasks record which worker ran them.
Failure behavior: Unregistered workers cannot receive tasks.

Title: Research worker
Requirement: A research worker executes market research, competitor research, and customer-segment analysis tasks producing cited documents.
User value: Core MVP value: real research output.
Evidence source: MVP definition; parity link: research capability observed in raw-audit/04 (labels)
Acceptance criteria: Produces structured research documents with sources for the three MVP research task types; outputs pass a usefulness review rubric.
Failure behavior: Source-unavailable findings are labeled unverified, never invented.

Title: Strategy worker
Requirement: A strategy worker executes business-model comparison and strategic-option generation tasks.
Acceptance criteria: Generates options meeting STRAT-002 standard; comparisons state criteria and tradeoffs.
Failure behavior: Insufficient input triggers a request for specific missing information.

Title: Document worker
Requirement: A document worker produces business plans, landing-page copy, and internal product requirements documents.
Acceptance criteria: Produces the three MVP document types in editable form with provenance.
Failure behavior: Quality-check failure returns a draft marked as needing revision.

Title: Least-privilege tool access
Requirement: Each worker can invoke only its allowlisted tools; allowlists are server-enforced.
Acceptance criteria: A worker invoking a non-allowlisted tool is rejected server-side and audited; allowlist changes are audited.
Failure behavior: Rejection does not crash the task; it fails that step with reason.

Title: Worker pause and disable
Requirement: Individual workers can be paused or disabled per company by the owner.
Acceptance criteria: Disabled workers receive no new tasks; their queued tasks are held visibly.
Failure behavior: Disable during execution triggers safe-stop per TASK-007.

Title: Tool registry
Requirement: All executable capabilities are registered tools with declared inputs, side-effect class, and risk category.
User value: Complete inventory of what the AI can do.
Acceptance criteria: Every executable action maps to a registered tool with a risk class; unregistered execution paths do not exist.
Failure behavior: Unknown tools cannot be invoked; attempts are audited.

Title: Tool-call records
Requirement: Every tool call records worker, task, arguments digest, policy decision, approval reference (if any), result, and receipt for external effects.
Acceptance criteria: 100% of tool calls have records; external writes require a stored receipt to claim success.
Failure behavior: Missing receipt marks the call outcome 'unconfirmed', never 'succeeded'.

Title: Server-side policy gate
Requirement: Every tool call passes a server-side policy evaluation before execution; the model cannot self-authorize.
Evidence source: Task principles 7 and 16-17; raw-audit/13-mvp-and-roadmap.md Gate C
Acceptance criteria: Policy engine decision precedes every execution; bypass attempts fail closed and are audited.
Failure behavior: Policy-engine unavailability blocks execution (fail closed), with owner notification.

Title: Action risk classification
Requirement: Every tool/action is classified: informational, internal-reversible, external, or sensitive-irreversible; classification drives default approval behavior.
Evidence source: Task instruction section 12; raw-audit/05-approval-matrix.md (Polsia's matrix mostly unknown)
Acceptance criteria: All registered tools carry a risk class; class changes require admin action and audit.
Failure behavior: Unclassified tools default to sensitive-irreversible (most restrictive).

Title: Approval request content
Requirement: An approval request shows: exact action, reason, expected result, recipient/destination, data used, cost, risk, reversibility, and preview where applicable.
Evidence source: raw-audit/09-claim-verification.md claim 25 (previews NOT verified in Polsia); task instruction
Acceptance criteria: All applicable fields render for each request type; missing fields block the request from being queued.
Failure behavior: Un-previewable actions state why and show the raw payload digest.

Title: Approval inbox
Requirement: Pending approvals appear in a dedicated inbox (surfaced in the Decision Room) with filtering and history.
Evidence source: polsia-audit-review.md correction 4 (no approval center demonstrated in Polsia)
Acceptance criteria: All pending requests appear within seconds; decided items move to history with decision metadata.
Failure behavior: Inbox outage blocks approval-gated execution (fail closed).

Title: Payload-bound approvals
Requirement: Approvals bind to a content hash of the exact action payload; any edit invalidates the approval and requires re-approval.
User value: What you approved is exactly what runs.
Acceptance criteria: Executing with a payload whose hash mismatches the approval is rejected server-side and audited; test proves edit-invalidates.
Failure behavior: Hash-check failure = rejection, never warn-and-continue.

Title: Approval expiration
Requirement: Approvals carry an expiry; expired approvals cannot execute.
Acceptance criteria: Expired approval attempts fail closed with a clear re-request path; default expiry per risk class.
Failure behavior: Clock issues resolve conservatively (treat as expired).

Title: Approval revocation
Requirement: An unexecuted approval can be revoked at any time; revocation takes effect before any subsequent execution attempt.
Acceptance criteria: Revoked approvals fail closed on execution attempts; revocation is audited with actor and time.
Failure behavior: Race between revoke and execute resolves in favor of revoke or produces a compensating alert.

Title: Approval decision options
Requirement: Approvers can approve, reject, edit-then-approve (rebinding the hash), schedule, or approve a limited batch.
Acceptance criteria: All five decision paths work; edit-then-approve creates a new bound payload; batch approvals enumerate exact members.
Failure behavior: Partial batch failures report per-member outcomes.

Title: Configurable autonomy levels
Requirement: The product defines five operating levels (recommend-only, draft-and-approve, approve-by-category, operate-within-limits, advanced autonomy) configurable per company; MVP ships levels 1-2 only.
Evidence source: polsia-audit-review.md (five formal levels NOT verified in Polsia); task instruction
Acceptance criteria: Level setting changes default approval behavior per risk class as documented; MVP enforces levels 1-2; levels 3-5 are visible but disabled with roadmap note.
Failure behavior: Invalid level configurations fall back to the most restrictive level.

Title: Server-authoritative enforcement
Requirement: Approval requirements are enforced at the execution layer, not the UI; no client state can authorize an action.
Acceptance criteria: API-level attempts to execute approval-gated actions without a valid approval are rejected; negative tests prove it.
Failure behavior: Enforcement-layer errors fail closed.

Title: Action previews
Requirement: External, paid, public, or destructive actions render a human-readable preview of exactly what will happen before approval.
Acceptance criteria: Preview matches executed output for previewable types (test-verified); non-previewable types are explicitly labeled.
Failure behavior: Preview generation failure blocks the approval request, not the safety.

Title: Spending limits
Requirement: Owners can set spending limits (per task, per day, per month, per category); the policy gate blocks execution beyond limits.
Evidence source: raw-audit/09-claim-verification.md claim 21 (only ad budgets documented in Polsia); task instruction
Acceptance criteria: Limit breach blocks execution with a clear message and escalation option; limits are audited on change.
Failure behavior: Ambiguous cost estimates reserve the worst case.

Title: Volume limits
Requirement: Owners can cap message counts, publishing frequency, and task volume per period.
Acceptance criteria: Caps enforce at the policy gate; counters are visible; caps change requires owner role.
Failure behavior: At-cap actions queue or fail per configured behavior, visibly.

Title: Approved channels and recipients
Requirement: Owners can restrict which channels and recipients/destinations the AI may contact.
User value: No surprises about where content goes.
Acceptance criteria: Non-approved destinations fail closed at policy evaluation; lists are auditable.
Failure behavior: Wildcard requests require explicit owner confirmation.

Title: Working-hours and scheduling limits
Requirement: Owners can define when autonomous work may run.
User value: Work happens when you want it to.
Evidence source: Task instruction; parity link: night-shift scheduling observed
Acceptance criteria: Out-of-window work does not start; in-flight work at window end follows safe-stop policy.
Failure behavior: Timezone changes re-evaluate schedules explicitly.

Title: Forbidden actions and escalation
Requirement: Owners can forbid specific actions/categories outright and define automatic escalation for boundary cases.
User value: Bright lines the AI cannot cross.
Acceptance criteria: Forbidden actions are rejected at the policy gate regardless of approval state; escalations create Decision Room items.
Failure behavior: Conflicts between policies resolve to the most restrictive.

Title: Policy evaluation record
Requirement: Every policy evaluation (allow/deny/escalate) is recorded with the policy version, inputs, and outcome.
Acceptance criteria: Every tool call links a policy evaluation record; records are immutable and queryable.
Failure behavior: Missing evaluation = execution blocked (fail closed).

Title: Deletion restrictions and required approvers
Requirement: Owners can require specific approvers for deletion and other designated high-impact categories.
Acceptance criteria: Configured categories require the designated approver; others cannot approve.
Failure behavior: Absent approver escalates rather than defaults open.

Title: Typed memory items
Requirement: Company memory is stored as typed items: facts, preferences, constraints, assumptions, research findings, decisions, outcomes, corrections.
Evidence source: raw-audit/09-claim-verification.md claim 27 (memory editor NOT found in Polsia)
Acceptance criteria: All eight types exist; every item has type, content, source link, timestamp, and status.
Failure behavior: Untyped writes are rejected.

Title: Memory visibility and control
Requirement: All memory items are visible, editable, and deletable by the owner.
User value: Nothing hidden about what the AI believes.
Acceptance criteria: A memory browser lists/filters all items; edits and deletions persist and are audited.
Failure behavior: Deletion propagates: dependent plans flag for review.

Title: Memory provenance
Requirement: Every memory item links to its source (interview answer, document, task result, user edit) and is company-scoped.
Acceptance criteria: 100% of items carry a resolvable source link and company scope; cross-company reads are impossible.
Failure behavior: Source-less legacy items are flagged 'unsourced', never presented as fact.

Title: Instruction precedence
Requirement: Memory can never silently override an explicit client instruction; conflicts surface as questions.
Acceptance criteria: A seeded memory/instruction conflict produces a surfaced question, not silent memory precedence; test-verified.
Failure behavior: Unresolvable conflicts pause the affected work.

Title: Company activity feed
Requirement: Every company has a chronological activity feed covering planning, task events, documents, and system actions.
Acceptance criteria: All significant events appear in order with timestamps; feed is filterable by type.
Failure behavior: Feed lag is visible ('as of' timestamp); no fabricated ordering.

Title: Append-only audit log
Requirement: All security-relevant events (auth, policy, approvals, tool calls, state changes, billing) are recorded in an append-only audit log.
Acceptance criteria: Audit records are immutable, include actor/timestamp/context, and are exportable; tamper attempts are detectable.
Failure behavior: Audit-write failure blocks the audited action (fail closed) for high-risk classes.

Title: Proposed vs executed distinction
Requirement: The UI always distinguishes proposed/planned work from executed work; nothing presented as done without an execution record.
Acceptance criteria: Visual and data-level distinction exists everywhere work is shown; claiming 'done' requires a run record (and receipt for external effects).
Failure behavior: Unconfirmed outcomes show 'unconfirmed', never 'completed'.

Title: Usage and credit visibility
Requirement: Credit and usage changes (grants, spends, refunds, expiry) are visible in a ledger with per-event linkage to causing tasks.
Acceptance criteria: Ledger shows every movement with cause link; balance always equals ledger sum.
Failure behavior: Discrepancies trigger automatic reconciliation alerts.

Title: Failure visibility
Requirement: Failures (tasks, provisioning, integrations) are first-class feed events with links to detail.
User value: Bad news travels fast, to you.
Evidence source: raw-audit/04-task-and-agent-system.md (Failed tab observed; detail absent in Polsia)
Acceptance criteria: Every failure emits a feed event linking the TASK-006 detail view.
Failure behavior: Suppressed notifications still leave the feed record.

Title: Website generation
Requirement: The platform can generate a public marketing website for a company.
Acceptance criteria: Generated site renders at a platform URL with navigation and CTA; content derives from the approved understanding/strategy.
Failure behavior: Generation failure leaves no half-published site; status is truthful.

Title: Application generation
Requirement: The platform can generate a working web application (beyond a static site) for a company.
Evidence source: raw-audit/22-exported-code-verification.md (one exported project verified: builds, tests pass)
Acceptance criteria: A generated application builds, passes its included tests, and deploys to a preview.
Failure behavior: Failed generations are visible with diagnostics; no broken deploys promoted.

Title: Source-code export
Requirement: Users can download the complete source of generated software.
Acceptance criteria: Export contains buildable source with config templates and no secret values; checksum and revision included.
Failure behavior: Export failure is reported; partial archives are never delivered silently.

Title: Masked secrets management
Requirement: Application secrets are managed through a masked UI; values are hidden by default, provided secrets are read-only, changes require redeploy to take effect.
Acceptance criteria: Secret values never render in plaintext by default nor appear in logs/exports; change-then-deploy flow works.
Failure behavior: Failed secret updates do not partially apply.

Title: Versioning and rollback
Requirement: Deployments are versioned; users can roll back to a prior version.
Evidence source: raw-audit/09-claim-verification.md claim 29 (rollback copy observed; no versions existed to test)
Acceptance criteria: Each deploy creates an immutable version; rollback redeploys a prior artifact and records outcome; rollback requires approval.
Failure behavior: Rollback failure preserves current version and alerts.

Title: Custom domains
Requirement: Users can view their platform URL and connect custom domains.
Evidence source: raw-audit/02-application-map.md (Manage Domains observed; no domain connected)
Acceptance criteria: Domain connection flow validates DNS, provisions TLS, and reports status truthfully.
Failure behavior: Misconfigured DNS shows actionable guidance.

Title: Generated-code quality gates
Requirement: Generated software must pass lint, typecheck, tests, and dependency-vulnerability scan before deployment is offered.
Acceptance criteria: Deploy is blocked until gates pass; gate results are visible per version.
Failure behavior: Gate failures produce actionable reports, not silent downgrades.

Title: Hosted deployment
Requirement: Generated sites/apps deploy to managed hosting with a stable platform URL and health status.
Acceptance criteria: Deployed artifact serves at its URL; health checks run; status shown truthfully.
Failure behavior: Unhealthy deploys are flagged; site status never claims healthy when down.

Title: Deployment approval and preview
Requirement: Production deployments of changed software require preview plus approval (per APPR risk class external).
Acceptance criteria: Production deploys without valid approval are rejected server-side; previews reflect the exact artifact.
Failure behavior: Preview-production drift blocks deploy.

Title: Company email surface
Requirement: Each company has an email identity with visible sent/received activity.
Acceptance criteria: Company email identity exists; sent/received counts and message log are visible.
Failure behavior: Delivery failures are visible per message.

Title: Outbound email controls
Requirement: Outbound email requires recipient validation, consent/policy checks, approval per risk class, and delivery receipts.
Acceptance criteria: No outbound email sends without policy pass + required approval; receipts stored; unsubscribe honored.
Failure behavior: Bounced/rejected messages are visible with reasons.

Title: Social publishing surface
Requirement: Companies can connect a social account and publish posts, with manual and scheduled ('auto-post') modes behind approval controls.
Evidence source: raw-audit/09-claim-verification.md claim 12 (social controls + public post observed, 99%)
Acceptance criteria: Connected account state is visible; publishing requires policy pass + approval per level; published posts store receipts/URLs.
Failure behavior: Publish failures surface with platform error context.

Title: Advertising with budget caps
Requirement: Companies can run ad campaigns with owner-set budget caps, explicit fees, approval, and stop controls.
Evidence source: raw-audit/07-billing-and-pricing.md (ads FAQ: budgets + 20% fee, 85%); not exercised
Acceptance criteria: Campaign creation requires budget cap and approval; spend halts at cap; fees are displayed before approval.
Failure behavior: Overspend attempts are blocked; cap breaches trigger immediate pause + alert.

Title: Customer-support assistance
Requirement: The platform can draft or handle customer-inquiry responses under configured autonomy and policies.
Acceptance criteria: Support replies obey autonomy level: draft-only by default; sends require approval unless a higher level is configured.
Failure behavior: Uncertain answers escalate to the owner rather than guessing.

Title: Customer payments surface
Requirement: Companies can accept customer payments through a managed balance with visible status and portal access.
Evidence source: raw-audit/07-billing-and-pricing.md (payments FAQ + Stripe portal observed; no payment executed, 85%)
Acceptance criteria: Payment setup state, balance, and payout path are visible; fees disclosed before enabling.
Failure behavior: Payment-provider failures never show phantom balances.
Open question: Fee model and money-movement compliance need owner + legal decisions (OQ-11, OQ-24).

Title: Subscription plan
Requirement: The platform offers a monthly subscription per account that includes one company, a scheduled-work allowance, and a task-credit allowance.
Evidence source: raw-audit/07-billing-and-pricing.md ($25/mo, 30 night shifts, 5 credits observed, 99%) — reference values, not our final pricing
Acceptance criteria: Subscription state gates paid features; plan contents are displayed accurately; cancellation follows BILL-006.
Failure behavior: Payment failure enters a documented dunning state without instant data loss.
Open question: Our actual pricing is an owner decision (D-02); Polsia values are reference evidence only.

Title: Task credits and ledger
Requirement: Manual task execution consumes task credits tracked in an append-only ledger with grants, spends, refunds, expirable/permanent split, and reset dates.
Evidence source: raw-audit/07-billing-and-pricing.md (credits dialog + ledger observed, 99%); raw-audit/24 (spend observed)
Acceptance criteria: Ledger is append-only; balance derives from ledger; concurrent final-credit race resolves to exactly one success (AT-025 pattern).
Failure behavior: Negative balances are impossible; reconciliation runs detect drift.

Title: Additional credit purchase
Requirement: Users can purchase additional task-credit tiers.
Evidence source: raw-audit/07-billing-and-pricing.md (tier selector observed, 99%) — tier prices are Polsia reference data
Acceptance criteria: Purchase flow grants credits atomically with payment confirmation; tiers display accurately.
Failure behavior: Failed payments grant nothing; no orphaned grants.

Title: Billing portal
Requirement: Users manage subscription and payment methods through a hosted billing portal (provider-neutral requirement).
Evidence source: raw-audit/02-application-map.md (portal entry observed, 99%) — Polsia uses Stripe; our provider is an architecture decision
Acceptance criteria: Portal reachable from settings; subscription changes reflect in-product within one minute.
Failure behavior: Portal unavailability shows status; no in-product stale claims.

Title: Additional-company pricing (UNRESOLVED)
Requirement: Accounts can add companies for an additional monthly fee. The reference product showed +$20/month (UI) and $25/month (FAQ) — contradiction C-02, deliberately unresolved. Our price is owner decision D-02.
Evidence source: evidence/pricing.csv row extra_company; raw-audit/24 section 2 (both values observed)
Acceptance criteria: Whatever price the owner sets displays identically in every surface (upgrade sheet, FAQ, checkout) — the reference product's inconsistency is the anti-pattern.
Failure behavior: Price display mismatch anywhere is a launch-blocking defect.
Open question: C-02: which value is Polsia's real price is unknown; both observations preserved.

Title: Cancellation semantics
Requirement: Cancelling a subscription pauses companies and preserves data rather than deleting it; deletion is a separate explicit action.
Acceptance criteria: Post-cancellation: no autonomous work, data intact, reactivation path documented; deletion still requires COMP-007 flow.
Failure behavior: Billing-state ambiguity resolves to paused-not-deleted.

Title: Usage metering with account rollups
Requirement: Every task run and significant tool call records an immutable company-level usage event attributable to company, account, and task. Account-level usage is a deterministic aggregation of company-level events across the account's companies.
User value: Accurate accounting foundation at both company and account level.
Evidence source: raw-audit/24 (credit decrement observed after run); ledger observed. Account-rollup clause: owner decision D-04/ADR-003 (2026-07-18) — clarification amendment, see PRD change log 1.2.0-draft
Acceptance criteria: Every run has immutable usage events reconciling to the ledger; per-company usage is queryable; per-account rollups aggregate deterministically with no double counting and reconcile to the sum of company events; corrections use compensating entries only; company moves/deactivations preserve historical attribution (test-covered).
Failure behavior: Metering failure blocks new metered work (fail closed) rather than under-billing silently; rollup drift is detected by reconciliation and repaired by rebuild from the event ledger.
Open question: Amended 2026-07-18: account-rollup clause added as a clarification of the approved ADR-003 control list (per-account usage recording), not a new product capability — the capability was owner-approved on 2026-07-18; this amendment aligns the requirement text with that decision.

Title: Cost preview and forecast
Requirement: Before execution users see estimated cost; owners can view usage trends and forecasts.
Acceptance criteria: Estimates shown pre-execution with stated uncertainty; monthly forecast visible; estimate-vs-actual tracked.
Failure behavior: Unestimable costs show 'unknown' and require explicit confirmation.

Title: Data and document export
Requirement: Users can export company data: documents, memory items, decisions, activity history, and configuration in documented formats.
Evidence source: raw-audit/09-claim-verification.md claim 18 (ownership terms NOT found in Polsia); competitive gap (portability)
Acceptance criteria: Export produces complete documented-format archives; contents match in-product data; no secret values included.
Failure behavior: Partial export failures enumerate what is missing.

Title: Portability manifest
Requirement: Exports include a manifest describing artifacts, formats, and (for software) reproducible build/deploy instructions independent of our platform.
Acceptance criteria: A third party can rebuild/redeploy exported software following only the manifest (verified in test).
Failure behavior: Non-portable elements are explicitly listed as such.

Title: Emergency stop hierarchy
Requirement: Owners can stop activity at every scope: task, worker, capability, integration, company, external-actions-only, and account-wide; stops take effect before the next tool call.
Evidence source: Task instruction; parity link: company Pause observed (raw-audit/02)
Acceptance criteria: Each scope's stop halts new tool calls at that scope within seconds; in-flight calls reach safe-stop; all stops are audited and reversible by the owner.
Failure behavior: Stop-system failure defaults to blocking execution platform-wide (fail closed).

Title: Recovery after reactivation
Requirement: Resuming from any stop/pause requires explicit review of held work before it executes; nothing auto-fires on resume.
Acceptance criteria: Held items are listed on resume; each requires confirm/discard; expired approvals are not resurrected.
Failure behavior: Unreviewed held items remain held indefinitely.

Title: Roles and membership
Requirement: The product defines roles (account owner, company owner, admin, operator, approver, viewer, billing admin); MVP ships account owner + viewer; invites are company-scoped.
Acceptance criteria: Role permissions match the §13 matrix; invites grant only the selected company; revocation is immediate and audited.
Failure behavior: Permission-check failures deny access (fail closed).

Title: Notifications
Requirement: Users receive configurable notifications for approvals needed, failures, completions, and spending events.
Acceptance criteria: Notification preferences per event class; delivery is logged; critical events (emergency, spend) cannot be fully silenced, only rerouted.
Failure behavior: Notification failure never blocks the underlying action's audit record.

Title: Connection manager
Requirement: A connection manager shows every connected external account: provider, account identity, granted scopes, health, last activity, and disconnect control.
Evidence source: raw-audit/06-integrations.md (Polsia exposed NO general connection manager)
Acceptance criteria: All connections appear with scopes and health; disconnect works immediately.
Failure behavior: Unknown-health connections show 'unverified', not 'healthy'.

Title: Credential vault references
Requirement: Integration credentials are stored server-side by reference; plaintext values are never returned by read APIs, logs, or exports.
Acceptance criteria: Negative tests prove no API/log/export path returns plaintext credentials.
Failure behavior: Vault unavailability blocks credential-using actions (fail closed).

Title: Revocation enforcement
Requirement: Disconnecting or revoking an integration immediately prevents all further use; queued work using it fails visibly.
Evidence source: raw-audit/06-integrations.md (revocation unknown in Polsia); launch gate requirement
Acceptance criteria: Post-revocation tool calls using the connection fail closed and are audited; test-verified.
Failure behavior: Race between revoke and in-flight call resolves to failure of the call or compensating alert.

Title: Tenant isolation
Requirement: Every persisted row and every query is company-scoped; cross-company access attempts fail closed and are audited. 100% of isolation test suite (AT-027 pattern) passes including adversarial ID substitution.
Acceptance criteria: Adversarial cross-tenant test suite passes 100%; denial responses do not leak resource existence.
Failure behavior: Any isolation test failure is a launch blocker.

Title: Server-authoritative authorization
Requirement: All authorization decisions execute server-side; UI state is never a security boundary. Negative tests cover every privileged endpoint.
Acceptance criteria: Every privileged endpoint has a negative authorization test; client-forged requests are rejected.
Failure behavior: Authz service failure denies by default.

Title: Availability
Requirement: Core dashboard and Decision Room target 99.5% monthly availability in beta; planned maintenance is announced and excluded.
Acceptance criteria: Availability is measured and reported monthly; misses trigger review.
Failure behavior: Degraded modes preserve read access where possible.

Title: Performance
Requirement: Dashboard first meaningful content under 2.5s p75 on warm sessions; interview question generation under 10s p90; long work is asynchronous with visible progress.
User value: Feels responsive despite heavy AI work.
Acceptance criteria: Metrics measured in production against stated targets.
Failure behavior: Slow operations show progress; nothing blocks the UI silently.

Title: Reliability and resumability
Requirement: All multi-step workflows (provisioning, planning, task runs) are resumable from checkpoints; no workflow loses state on process restart.
Acceptance criteria: Kill-and-resume tests pass for every workflow type; no orphaned resources after crash-resume.
Failure behavior: Unresumable states are detected and surfaced for manual recovery.

Title: Idempotency
Requirement: All external side effects carry idempotency keys; replay/duplicate-trigger tests produce zero duplicate external effects.
Acceptance criteria: Replay test suite shows zero duplicates across all external tool types.
Failure behavior: Detected duplicates are suppressed and raised as incidents.

Title: Retry discipline
Requirement: Retries use bounded exponential backoff with per-class caps; retry state is visible (TASK-010); dead-lettered work is surfaced to owner.
Acceptance criteria: Retry behavior matches configured policy in tests; dead letters appear in Decision Room blocked queue.
Failure behavior: Retry storms are impossible by config cap.

Title: Auditability
Requirement: 100% of security-relevant events produce immutable audit records within 5 seconds; audit export covers any date range.
Acceptance criteria: Audit completeness test: every action type in the registry produces its record; export verified.
Failure behavior: Audit lag beyond threshold alerts operators.

Title: Observability
Requirement: All services emit structured logs (secret-redacted), metrics, and traces; every task run is traceable end-to-end by ID.
Acceptance criteria: A task ID resolves to a complete trace; log secret-scanning finds zero hits in CI.
Failure behavior: Telemetry loss degrades gracefully; never blocks user work.

Title: Security baseline
Requirement: OWASP ASVS-aligned controls: input validation, output encoding, CSRF protection, rate limiting, dependency scanning in CI, and third-party pen review before public beta.
Acceptance criteria: CI gates enforce dependency and static scanning; pen-test findings at high+ severity are closed before beta.
Failure behavior: Known-vulnerable dependencies block deploy.

Title: Privacy
Requirement: Personal data is encrypted in transit and at rest; data map and retention schedule exist before beta; users can export and request deletion; no personal data in logs.
Acceptance criteria: Data map covers all stores; deletion requests complete within stated SLA; log scans show zero personal-data hits.
Failure behavior: Retention conflicts resolve to the stricter rule.

Title: Accessibility
Requirement: Core flows meet WCAG 2.1 AA: keyboard navigable, screen-reader labeled, color-independent state indicators.
Acceptance criteria: Automated a11y checks in CI plus manual audit of the five core journeys.
Failure behavior: A11y regressions block release of affected surfaces.

Title: Maintainability
Requirement: Codebase enforces typed interfaces, module boundaries, CI lint/typecheck/test gates, and per-module ownership documentation.
Acceptance criteria: CI gates green on every merge; module docs exist for each domain.
Failure behavior: Gate failures block merge.

Title: Portability
Requirement: User-facing outputs (documents, data, generated code) export in open formats; no user artifact is locked to proprietary formats.
Acceptance criteria: Every artifact type has a documented open export format.
Failure behavior: Non-exportable artifact types cannot ship.

Title: Cost control
Requirement: Per-task and per-company AI spend is metered with hard caps; a runaway task cannot exceed its budget by more than one billing increment.
Acceptance criteria: Budget-cap tests show enforcement within one increment; spend dashboards reconcile with provider bills.
Failure behavior: Cap breaches halt the task and alert.

Title: Data retention
Requirement: Retention periods per data class are documented and enforced; deletion honors retention exceptions transparently.
Acceptance criteria: Automated retention jobs run and log; exceptions are user-visible.
Failure behavior: Retention-job failure alerts; nothing purges without a log.

Title: Backup and recovery
Requirement: Databases are backed up with tested restore; RPO ≤ 24h and RTO ≤ 4h for beta; restore drills run before beta and quarterly.
Acceptance criteria: A documented restore drill succeeds within the stated RTO.
Failure behavior: Backup failures alert within one cycle.

Title: Secret handling
Requirement: All platform and user secrets live in a managed secret store, referenced not copied; secrets never appear in logs, error messages, browser responses, or exports (CI-scanned).
Acceptance criteria: Secret-scanning in CI and log pipelines shows zero findings; negative tests on API responses pass.
Failure behavior: Detected exposure triggers immediate rotation runbook.

Title: Model-provider resilience
Requirement: AI provider outages degrade gracefully: work queues rather than fails permanently, users see honest status, and provider failover is possible by configuration (no single hardwired vendor).
Acceptance criteria: Simulated provider outage: tasks queue, status is honest, recovery drains the queue without duplicates.
Failure behavior: Extended outages notify owners with options.

Title: Integration failure handling
Requirement: External integration failures are isolated per connection: one failing provider cannot stall unrelated work; failures surface health status and recovery guidance.
User value: One bad link doesn't break the chain.
Acceptance criteria: Fault-injection tests show isolation; health status updates within one check cycle.
Failure behavior: Cascading-failure detection pauses only the affected scope.

Title: Prompt-injection defense
Requirement: Content from external sources (web, email, social) is treated as untrusted data: it cannot invoke tools, alter policies, or claim user authority; tool calls triggered while processing external content face heightened policy scrutiny.
User value: The outside world can't hijack your AI team.
Acceptance criteria: Injection test corpus (instructions embedded in researched web content) produces zero unauthorized tool executions.
Failure behavior: Suspected injection quarantines the content and flags the task.
